title: Paucuckatux (Tom's Creek)
summary: Paucuckatux is identified as a creek on the bounds of Hashamomuk Neck in Southold, probably the stream known as Tom's Creek.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Tom's Creek / Hashamomuck Pond landscape point based on Tooker location; not an exact historical creek or boundary coordinate. Offset slightly from Patchummuck for map visibility.
history_content: The placename belongs to the Southold boundary landscape around Hashamomuk Neck, Tom's Creek, and nearby pond and cove settings. Land-transfer and boundary details appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as a divided creek or divided tidal river. Related historical spellings include Paucackatun, Pautuckatux, and Paugetuck.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names are rich in meaning: they impart traditional knowledge of the land, its geography and its natural resources. They also communicate Indigenous worldviews, stories and teachings.”

— Natural Resources Canada, Honouring the teachings of these lands (2024), Indigenous place names section
whereintheworld_content: Approximate/general point near the Tom's Creek and Hashamomuck Pond landscape in Southold. This is not an exact historical creek-head or boundary coordinate.
